title: Policy benchmark: fixed vs compute-only vs cooling-only vs independent vs joint
research_question: How much facility energy per successful task does each control strategy save relative to a fixed conventional policy, and does joint compute-cooling optimisation save more than energy-aware compute and cooling controllers running independently?
hypothesis: H1: joint uses less energy per successful task than independent in at least 4 of 6 scenarios (paired 95% CI entirely below 0), without more SLO violations or thermal-limit exceedances. H2: every optimising policy uses less energy per successful task than fixed in every scenario.
null_hypothesis: Joint and independent do not differ (CI includes 0) or differ by less than the practical threshold.
controlled_variables: thermal target 80 C / hardware throttle 85 C
baseline: fixed: full clock when busy, 18 C supply, design flow
configuration: 8 accelerators on one liquid loop; dry cooler + trim chiller; see parameter registry
evaluation_criteria: Primary: paired relative difference in E_per_success_kJ. A difference is 'meaningful' only if the whole 95% CI lies beyond 1%. Quality guard: success_rate and SLO violations must not worsen relative to the comparator. Thermal guard: zero chip-seconds throttled.
known_limitations: Synthetic workload (class F); controller has a perfect model of the plant; quasi-steady plant without loop thermal mass; single node; constant ambient per scenario.
data_collection: Simulator outputs written to the append-only SQLite store; every metric labelled with provenance; per-run config SHA-256 and code SHA-256 recorded; time series for selected seeds.
statistics: Paired by seed (identical workload realisation across levels). Per-seed relative difference d=(A-B)/B; mean with two-sided 95% Student-t CI.
